public_rationale: Reporting supports multibillion-dollar annual net losses. The $655 billion requirement remains unverified on the stated scope and period. CNBC's compute-only projection through 2030 is not a measure of all bills over the next five years. It would be unfair to treat that different figure as a contradiction, or to treat evidence of losses as support for the entire claim.
limitations: The claim combines two financial metrics that cannot be represented by one comparable total.
No primary financial schedule establishing the five-year requirement was available in the readable sources.
A spending projection is not automatically a binding payment obligation or an external financing requirement.

our_interpretation: Assess the spending requirement or projection that existed when the post appeared, rather than whether future spending has already occurred.
The plain reading of all its bills is gross company-wide expenditure, not an external financing gap after revenue.
Read next five years literally as February 26, 2026 through February 26, 2031; a calendar 2026–2030 budget is a plausible alternative but is not identical.
Use calendar 2025 for the annual-loss component because the surrounding passage explicitly discusses 2025 results.
The observation window includes the described 2025 loss year and the spending-plan snapshot on February 26, 2026.
The single contract metric_scope records the quantified spending requirement. Annual net losses are a separate component and require separately scoped evidence.
criteria.support_condition: A contemporaneous, complete spending schedule or credible financial projection establishes approximately $655 billion of company-wide bills over the stated five years, and comparable annual results establish multibillion-dollar net losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes a materially different total requirement over the same five years, or establishes that the described annual net losses did not occur. A different compute-only budget does not by itself contradict total bills.
